voyage-code-4 capability verification and batch-cap observation
==========================================================================

Date issued: 2026-08-25
Issued by:   the operator holding the Voyage key, from the local environment.
Spend:       deliberate, once. Call 1 billed 1 token. Call 2 was REJECTED
             before any embedding work, so it billed nothing.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The Voyage docs embeddings table lists voyage-code-4
with 256/512/1024/2048 dimensions and float|int8|uint8|binary|ubinary
dtypes, but the REST reference — the page that enumerates per-model dtype
support — does not list voyage-code-4 in ANY enumeration. Documentation
could not settle whether the model actually serves ubinary at 256. One real
API call settles it. This is that call, recorded verbatim.

The Authorization header is written below EXACTLY as
"Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***". The real key was read from the
operator's config, passed to curl through a 0600 header file (never through
argv, never echoed), and the file was deleted at the end of the run.


CALL 1 — CAPABILITY
-------------------

Command as issued:

    curl -sS -o resp1.json -w '%{http_code}\n' \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data-binary @body1.json \
      https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings

body1.json:

    {"input":["package main"],"model":"voyage-code-4","input_type":"document","output_dimension":256,"output_dtype":"ubinary"}

Raw status: 200

Raw response body (verbatim):

    {"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","embedding":[11,215,108,15,54,253,19,128,37,66,86,122,72,184,50,147,219,246,79,110,250,248,6,9,22,70,168,24,61,58,198,86],"index":0,"text":null}],"model":"voyage-code-4","usage":{"total_tokens":1}}

Decoded observations:

    len(data[0].embedding) = 32
    first 8 values          = [11, 215, 108, 15, 54, 253, 19, 128]
    every element an int    = true
    every element in 0..255 = true
    model echoed by the API = voyage-code-4
    usage.total_tokens      = 1

CONCLUSION, CALL 1: PASS. voyage-code-4 serves output_dtype ubinary at
output_dimension 256 and returns exactly 32 uint8 values — 256 bits at one
bit per dimension, the same width and representation the current default
model produces. The docs table is correct for this combination and the REST
reference's omission of the model is an incompleteness in that page, not a
missing capability.


CALL 2 — BATCH TOKEN CAP
------------------------

Command as issued:

    curl -sS -o resp2.json -w '%{http_code}\n' \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data-binary @body2.json \
      https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings

body2.json was a deliberately oversized batch: 128 inputs of ~20,000
characters each (2,562,437 bytes on the wire), same model/input_type/
output_dimension/output_dtype as call 1. 128 inputs is under any published
per-request ITEM cap, so a rejection isolates the TOTAL-TOKEN cap.

Raw status: 400

Raw response body (verbatim):

    {"detail":"Request to model 'voyage-code-4' failed. The max allowed tokens per submitted batch is 320000. Your batch has 320914 tokens after truncation. Please lower the number of tokens in the batch.","error_code":"TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH"}

CONCLUSION, CALL 2: the API DID disclose a numeric cap. voyage-code-4's
maximum total tokens per submitted batch is 320000, counted AFTER per-item
truncation. The error_code is TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH — the same literal
the client's overflow detector matches on, so the existing pack-and-bisect
recovery path recognizes this rejection unchanged.


WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE
----------------------------------

batchTokenBudget STAYS AT 100_000 and is NOT re-derived from the number
above. That is deliberate, not an oversight: the budget bounds packs for
the model actually in use, and the default model is NOT changing in this
changeset (the default flip is blocked on the embed cache key — see the
DefaultModel comment in ../voyage.go). 100_000 is the conservative budget
derived against the CURRENT default model's 120k cap. Raising it to a
code-4-derived figure would describe a model the client is not talking to,
which is the exact error this verification exists to avoid.

The 320000 figure is recorded here as the input a future re-derivation
needs, at the moment the default model flips. Note it is more than 2.6x the
current default's cap, so a flip that carries the budget over unchanged is
merely conservative — under-packing, never over-packing — and the
bisection path recovers from an under-estimate anyway.

No default model changed as a result of this verification.
